items.title: Apple earnings: iPhone prices are 'not immune' to rising memory costs
items.summary: Apple (AAPL) stock is stumbling in Thursday's after-hours since reporting fiscal third quarter earnings and revenue that topped estimates, carried by strong iPhone sales. New Street Research technology Infrastructure analyst Antoine Chkaiban explains the problem areas that could emerge down the line for Apple tied to the memory chip shortage.

items.title: Qualcomm's automotive segment is the highlight of Q3: CFO
items.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) CFO and COO Akash Palkhiwala sits down with Josh Lipton and Dan Howley on Market Domination to discuss the company's performance and outlook in various segments, including AI data centers and automotives.

items.title: Qualcomm’s Next Growth Engine Could Send Shares Much Higher
items.summary: Qualcomm's stock just took a brutal post-earnings hit despite beating revenue estimates, and the reason the market sold off so hard tells you almost nothing about where this company is actually headed.

items.title: Rivian Sinks 8% Despite Q2 Beat and Raised Guidance; Lucid Falls 6%
items.summary: Rivian just posted its cleanest quarterly beat in months and lifted full-year guidance, so why are shareholders waking up to an 8% drop while Lucid bleeds in sympathy and Tesla quietly holds its ground?

items.title: Broadcom No Longer Sells Itself As A Chip Cycle Story
items.summary: The business management once framed around a cyclical bottom is still growing, but it now gets a paragraph while artificial intelligence gets the company.

items.title: Qualcomm Stock's Biggest Risk Is The Gap Between Pain And Payoff
items.summary: Just over half of revenue still leans on a shrinking handset market, and the businesses meant to replace it do not reach their targeted scale for years.

items.title: Intel Stock's Operating Margin Turned Positive While Its Foundry Kept Losing Money
items.summary: Intel swung from an operating loss to an operating profit with the costly part of its turnaround still running, and that swing is what the spending debate keeps drowning out.

items.title: QCOM Q2 Deep Dive: Data Center and Automotive Growth Offset Smartphone Headwinds
items.summary: Wireless chipmaker Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) reported Q2 CY2026 results exceeding the market’s revenue expectations, but sales fell by 4% year on year to $9.95 billion. Guidance for next quarter’s revenue was better than expected at $10.1 billion at the midpoint, 1% above analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $2.21 per share was in line with analysts’ consensus estimates.
